clue.text: 16 go further ahead

definitions.meaning: to give a dog a clear view of its quarry you let it run out further on the leash
in a race, to increase the margin by which you are in front

explanation.walkthrough: 16 is the linked answer at 16 and 10 Down, the hunting phrase about letting the dog see its quarry; slackening the leash does exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog on a longer leash gets further forward, and a leader who extends the margin goes further ahead in a contest.

clue.text: Female model left with £25 for a horse

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
the Model T was Ford's famous car
and means together with
a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.surface: Someone buys a horse for twenty-five pounds from a woman who models.
explanation.walkthrough: A PONY is British betting slang for £25, so the money is part of the wordplay, not the price.
explanation.definitionFit: This small, sturdy breed from the Scottish northern isles is a type of horse.

clue.text: Horse eating a quarter of a tree

indicators.note: the horse takes a letter inside it, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed colours
W, for west, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A horse is munching part of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, with red berries, is a tree also called by this name.

clue.text: Cricketer, nurse and student in this country have a right

parts.note: to nurse is to tend

indicators.note: the student's letter sits inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: UK, the setter's country, a British paper
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A sportsman, a nurse and a student in Britain are all owed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this country' means the United Kingdom, where the paper is published.
explanation.definitionFit: Sachin, the Indian batting great, is perhaps the most famous cricketer of his generation.

clue.text: He will cut corners in his haste to make …

definitions.text: He will cut corners in his haste to make …

parts.words: He will cut corners in his haste to make
parts.note: read on into the next clue: someone who rushes and cuts corners to get ahead is a pushy, sharp operator

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into 5 Down: he cuts corners in his rush to make headway.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler or pushy go-getter hurries people along and cuts corners to get ahead.

clue.text: … progress, cape style

parts.note: a headland or cape, as in Beachy Head
a way of doing something is its style

explanation.surface: Following on from 4 Down: getting ahead in the manner of a coastal promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: Making ground towards a goal is progress, a nautical term for a ship's forward motion.

clue.text: It's clear the police need a bit of luck

indicators.note: only a piece of the word luck is wanted, its opening two letters

parts.note: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department, its detective branch

explanation.surface: It is obvious the detectives could do with some good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The police come first in the clue but last in the answer: the detectives 'need' the luck in front of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid writing or thinking is clear and easy to follow.

clue.text: Writer's got it — "unknown power"

parts.note: an author is a writer
Y is a stock algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An author quotes a phrase about some mysterious force.
explanation.definitionFit: Authority is the power or right to give orders and make decisions.

clue.text: Boy from the West in Scottish burgh

indicators.note: the compass letter is put inside the name of the city

parts.note: Edin is the old poetic short name of Edinburgh (Dun Edin)
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A lad from the west of Scotland in a burgh there.
explanation.walkthrough: Edinburgh was popularly said to be named after this Northumbrian king, so the boy is literally 'in' the burgh's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a boy's given name, borne by an early English king.

clue.text: Lack of transport in southern town

indicators.note: the vehicle goes inside the other two pieces

parts.note: a city is a large town
a car is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Complaining about poor transport in a town in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortage or dearth of something is a lack of it.

clue.text: See 16
A gull in trouble about speech

indicators.note: trouble means disorder or upset, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A seabird in difficulty is making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the indicator 'in trouble', but it is fodder: A GULL IN supplies all seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything to do with the tongue or with speaking.

clue.text: Where 27 agreed with Guthrum to take extra wives

definitions.meaning: the Somerset place where King Alfred made his treaty with the Danish leader Guthrum in 878
to marry more women, read as two words

explanation.surface: A king makes a pact with a Viking and starts collecting brides.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is Alfred the Great; the Treaty with Guthrum is named after a village in Somerset, a county in south-west England. Split it to get WED MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treaty of this Somerset village divided England between Saxons and Danes after Alfred's victory.

clue.text: City of moment in religion, as I know well

indicators.note: the city's name is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of a city that matters in faith, as they know well.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across religioN AS I Know.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian city of importance is a holy Hindu site that hosts the Kumbh Mela.

clue.text: On Day 1, two states are like Lilliput

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
the Roman numeral I is one
RI is Rhode Island and Cal is California, two US states
RI is Rhode Island and Cal is California, two US states

explanation.surface: On the first of the month two countries say they resemble a tiny kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Lilliput is Swift's land of tiny people in Gulliver's Travels, a mocking portrait of English politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift invented the miniature kingdom to mock the court of his day, so it is satirical in spirit.

clue.text: Moneymaker to go with new King Edwards?

definitions.meaning: the British institution that makes the coins

definitions.text: to go with new King Edwards?
definitions.meaning: King Edward is a potato variety; a royal herb, mint, is served with new potatoes

explanation.surface: A coin maker proposes a pairing with the next monarchs named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a popular British potato; new potatoes are traditionally boiled with mint, and 'King' makes the mint royal.
explanation.definitionFit: The national mint of Britain strikes the coins, so it is literally a maker of money.

clue.text: Facilitate hunting after time in oblivion — act — take part — be very angry inside

indicators.note: the letter for time goes inside the river of oblivion

parts.note: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth
to do is to act

indicators.note: the word for fuming goes inside the word for seizing

parts.note: to grab is to take
to seethe is to be furious
a bit is a part

explanation.surface: A series of instructions on hunting, acting, and fury, delivered in fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' simply links the definition to the wordplay; the hunting phrase means giving someone a fair chance before acting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to give someone a fair chance, as a hunting dog must glimpse its quarry before the chase.

clue.text: 'Perpetual Motion' by Rubens

indicators.note: motion means movement, so the letters are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: The title of a painting by the Flemish master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' stirs PERPETUAL into the painter's forenames.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubens's first names were Peter Paul, so they stand for the Flemish painter himself.

clue.text: Not easy to give prize without some power

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the prize surrounds the other piece

parts.note: an award is a prize
kW, kilowatt, is a unit measuring an amount of power

explanation.surface: Handing over a prize with no energy is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clumsy or difficult to handle is not easy to deal with.

clue.text: Walk to Canterbury for 2?

definitions.meaning: the ... Walk is a famous Cockney dance and song
the London palace of the Archbishop of Canterbury, then Rowan Williams, the answer at 2 Down

explanation.walkthrough: 2 Down is ROWAN, as in Rowan Williams, Archbishop of Canterbury at the time; his London residence is Lambeth Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The London borough gives its name to a dance and to the palace of the Archbishop of Canterbury.

clue.text: Herb for solver's crossword setter

parts.note: the setter addresses the solver as you, so 'your' in old form, thy
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A herb is offered to the solver by the person who made the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic garden plant is a common culinary herb.

clue.text: Wash here and not with some following the king

parts.note: nor means and not

indicators.note: only part of the word following is wanted, its opening three letters

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions say not here, with some followers of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wash is a bay on England's east coast bordering this county, so 'Wash' is a place, not laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wash, a large bay, lies along this county's coast.

clue.text: 'e makes footwear from a tree

indicators.note: the Cockney dropped H of he signals the same H dropped from the trade name

parts.note: a hosier makes or sells stockings and socks

explanation.surface: A Cockney fellow makes shoes from wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A HOSIER deals in hosiery; said with a Cockney dropped H it becomes the willow.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow whose pliant twigs are used in basket-making.

clue.text: Obsession about house plant

indicators.note: the obsession goes round the other piece

parts.note: a mania is an obsession

explanation.surface: Someone obsessed with a houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen shrub with yellow flowers is a garden plant.

clue.text: "Time for a word" is unAnglican

definitions.meaning: the present occasion, as in 'for the ___', and the word coined for one occasion
read as ..., not Church of England

explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England, so 'non-CE' is not Anglican.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonce word is coined for one occasion, and 'for the nonce' means for the time being.

clue.text: Part of Shakespeare play before tea break is put into operation

parts.note: Act IV, the fourth act, is part of any five-act play

indicators.note: breaking the word tea shatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Part of a Shakespeare drama is staged before an interval for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like an interval but scrambles TEA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To activate a device is to set it working, putting it into operation.

clue.text: Valley-born star

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley

explanation.surface: A star who was born in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: This bright star in Cygnus is one of the most luminous known.

clue.text: Father Ted with regal (rather than culinary) qualification?

definitions.text: Father Ted with regal (rather than culinary) qualification?

indicators.note: the letters are modified, qualified, into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Imagining the TV priest given a royal title rather than a cooking certificate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualification' mixes FATHER TED and REGAL. Alfred famously burnt the cakes, so his title praises his kingship, not his cooking. Father Ted is an Irish TV sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saxon king earned his title as a ruler, not as a cook after the legend of the burnt cakes.
